extraction.name: CoNLL-2003 Named Entity Recognition Dataset
extraction.description: The CoNLL-2003 shared task dataset for language-independent named entity recognition, covering English and German. It contains training, development, and test splits for each language with named entity annotations for persons, locations, organizations, and miscellaneous entities, along with large unannotated data files. The English data is sourced from the Reuters Corpus and the German data from the Frankfurter Rundschau newspaper.
extraction.creator: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang; Fien De Meulder
extraction.citeAs: Erik F. Tjong Kim Sang and Fien De Meulder. 2003. Introduction to the CoNLL-2003 Shared Task: Language-Independent Named Entity Recognition. In Proceedings of CoNLL-2003.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: English data was taken from the Reuters Corpus, consisting of Reuters news stories. German data was taken from the ECI Multilingual Text Corpus, specifically from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau. Data files were selected for training, development, test, and unannotated sets from specific time periods within these corpora.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Reuters Corpus (Reuters news stories from August 1996 to August 1997) for English data; ECI Multilingual Text Corpus (texts from the German newspaper Frankfurter Rundschau, 1992) for German data.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: English: August 1996 to December 1996 (training/development/test), September 1996 (unannotated); German: end of August 1992 (training/development/test), September to December 1992 (unannotated)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp, mostly following MUC conventions. Four entity types were annotated: persons (PER), organizations (ORG), locations (LOC), and miscellaneous names (MISC), using the IOB tagging scheme.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MBT memory-based tagger (for English POS tagging and chunking); Treetagger decision tree tagger (for German lemmatization, POS tagging, and chunking)
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Named entities are assumed to be non-recursive and non-overlapping; when a named entity is embedded in another named entity, usually only the top level entity has been annotated; the MISC category is described as a very diverse category covering adjectives, events, and other names not fitting the other three types
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluation of language-independent named entity recognition systems; developing machine learning components for named entity recognition in English and German; benchmarking and comparing different learning methods for named entity recognition
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For all data, a tokenizer, part-of-speech tagger, and a chunker were applied to the raw data. Two basic language-specific tokenizers were created. The English data was tagged and chunked by the memory-based MBT tagger. The German data was lemmatized, tagged and chunked by the decision tree tagger Treetagger. Named entity tagging of English and German training, development, and test data was done by hand at the University of Antwerp, mostly following MUC conventions.
